title: Childcare subsidy eligibility and household income assessment
asked: The MP asked whether the Ministry will review how gross monthly household income and per capita income are computed so that young parents living in their parents’ or relatives’ properties can exclude other family members’ income, and whether caregiving expenses for elderly dependents can be factored into Additional Subsidy eligibility for childcare.
response: Mr Goh Pei Ming said ECDA uses gross monthly household income to assess means-tested additional subsidy, looking only at both parents' income and not other household members. Larger families with five or more household members can be means tested on a per capita basis, using all household members' income divided by the number of members, and receive the more favourable result. In supplementary answers, he said ECDA and MSF are in close contact with preschools, family service centres and social service agencies, and will make necessary changes when feedback is received.

key_points.point: ECDA assesses means-tested additional subsidy using gross monthly household income.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: uses the gross monthly household income to assess the amount of means tested additional subsidy

key_points.point: The assessment looks only at both parents' income and excludes other household members' income.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: looks only at the income of both parents of a child in the family and does not include the income of other family members in the household

key_points.point: Families with five or more household members can be means tested on a per capita basis.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: we do allow for larger families with five or more household members to be means tested on a per capita basis

key_points.point: Per capita income is all household members' income divided by the total number of household members.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: computed using the income of all the family members in the household, divided by the total number of family members in the household

key_points.point: Such families get the more favourable means-tested result of the two processes.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: such families would receive the more favourable means tested result of the two processes

key_points.point: ECDA and MSF are in close contact with preschools, family service centres and social service agencies.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: ECDA and MSF are in close contact with the preschools, as well as in close contact with the various family service centres and social service agencies on the ground

key_points.point: The Ministry will make necessary changes when it receives feedback.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: We will not shy away from making necessary changes when we do get some feedback

left_open: Whether the Ministry will review the computational method for gross monthly household income and per capita income for young parents residing in their parents’ or relatives’ properties.
Whether caregiving expenses for elderly dependents will be factored into eligibility assessments for Additional Subsidy for childcare.
A timeline for any planned review of subsidy eligibility frameworks affecting young families.
supplementary: Feedback from social service agencies on eligibility criteria and timelines for reviewing subsidy frameworks for young families.
